items.title: JCODE: Rust Tabanlı AI Agent Harness Mimarisi
items.summary:
JCODE: Rust Tabanlı AI Agent Harness Mimarisi
Performans Benchmarking, Mimari Derin İnceleme, Kurulum Rehberi ve Topluluk Eleştirileri

1. Giriş ve Genel Bakış

Yazılım geliştirme süreçlerinde Büyük Dil Modellerinin (LLM) doğrudan terminal üzerinden kullanılması, Claude Code gibi araçların yaygınlaşmasıyla yeni bir boyut kazandı. Ancak Node.js ve JavaScript tabanlı bu harness
sistemleri, yüksek bellek tüketimi (300 MB - 600 MB) ve başlatma sürelerindeki gecikmeler (3+ saniye) nedeniyle geliştiricilerin tepkisini çekmektedir.

Geliştirici Jesse Huang ( 1jehuang ) tarafından açık kaynak olarak yayınlanan jcode, terminal üzerinde çalışan sıfır bağımlılıklı, yüksek performanslı bir AI agent arayüzüdür. Saf Rust diliyle yazılmış olan proje, Claude Code mimarisine kıyasla 245 kat daha hızlı ilk yanıt süresi (TTTF) ve son derece düşük sistem kaynağı kullanımı vaat etmektedir.

2. Teknik Benchmark ve Mimarinin Karşılaştırılması

Resmi test sonuçları ve bağımsız doğrulama verilerine göre jcode ile mevcut popüler çözümler arasındaki temel teknik farklar aşağıdaki tabloda özetlenmiştir: 

Benden Ufak Bir Not: Agent Harness Nedir?

jcode kendisi bir yapay zeka modeli değildir. OpenAI (GPT-4o), Anthropic (Claude 3.5/3.7), Google (Gemini) ve yerel modeller (Ollama) gibi 30'dan fazla model sağlayıcısını bağlayan, komut çalıştırma, dosya okuma/yazma ve
semantik hafıza yönetimini üstlenen TUI (Terminal User Interface) katmanıdır. 

3. Öne Çıkan Mimari Özellikler

Agent Swarm Yönetimi: Tek bir kod deposu (repository) üzerinde birden fazla agent'ın aynı anda çalışmasına izin verir. Agent'lar kendi aralarında mesajlaşabilir ve çakışan kod değişikliklerini (diff) anlık olarak algılar. Semantik Vektör Hafızası (SpecMem): Düz metin not defterleri yerine konuşma geçmişini vektör gömmelerine (embeddings) dönüştürerek ilgili bağlamı otomatik çeker.

Session Persistence (Oturum Sürdürme): Kesilen veya yarım kalan çalışmayı, durum kaybı olmadan kaldığı yerden devam ettirme olanağı sağlar.

4. Eleştirel Yaklaşım ve Topluluk Tartışmaları

Jcode sunduğu olağanüstü performans rakamlarıyla dikkat çekse de, geliştirici topluluğunda ve teknik forumlarda bazı ciddi eleştirilerle karşı karşıyadır:

A. Kod Aşırmak (Plagiarism) ve Açık Kaynak Etiği
Reddit ( r/ClaudeCode ) ve GitHub tartışmalarında, projenin semantik hafıza ve agent koordinasyon mimarisinin diğer açık kaynak projelerden ve LLM çıktıları yardımıyla kopyalanıp Rust'a doğrudan port edildiği öne sürülmüştür. Katkı sağlayan ilk geliştiricilere lisans atıfı yapılmaması açık kaynak etiği açısından soru işaretleri yaratmaktadır.

B. RAM Kullanımındaki "Pazarlama Rakamları"
Öne çıkarılan 27.8 MB RAM değeri, projenin en önemli özelliği olan yerel semantik gömme (local embedding) özelliği tamamen kapatıldığında geçerlidir. Lokal vektör hafızası aktif edildiğinde bellek tüketimi **167 MB**
seviyelerine yükselmektedir. Yine de Node.js alternatiflerine göre hafif olsa da pazarlama söylemi ile gerçek dünya kullanımı arasında fark mevcuttur.

C. Erken Aşama Hataları ve Stabilite
Projenin GitHub deposunda 100'ün üzerinde açık issue (hata bildirimi) yer almaktadır. Özellikle karmaşık OAuth doğrulama adımlarında, bazı LLM sağlayıcılarının token sınırlarında ve uç durumlardaki Swarm kilitlenmelerinde
kararsızlıklar yaşandığı rapor edilmiştir. 

5. Detaylı Kurulum ve Kullanım Rehberi

Adım 1: Sistem Gereksinimleri ve Hazırlık
jcode statik bir Rust binary'si olarak derlendiği için sisteminizde Rust araç zincirinin (Rustup) kurulu olması önerilir.

# Rust yükleme (Linux/macOS)
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://t.co/ZR3uVSGhvV | sh

# Versiyon kontrolü
rustc --version

Adım 2: jcode Kurulumu
Depoyu klonlayarak veya Cargo paket yöneticisi üzerinden doğrudan kurabilirsiniz:

# Cargo ile doğrudan kurulum
cargo install jcode

# Alternatif: Kaynak koddan derleme
git clone https://t.co/JJVCTev4DN
cd jcode
cargo build --release
sudo cp target/release/jcode /usr/local/bin/

Adım 3: Model ve API Key Yapılandırması
Kullanmak istediğiniz API sağlayıcısının anahtarını ortam değişkeni olarak tanımlayabilirsiniz:

# Anthropic Claude API
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-api..."
# OpenAI API
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-proj-..."
# Google Gemini API
export GEMINI_API_KEY="AIzaSy..."

Adım 4: Proje Dizininde Başlatma

# Çalışmak istediğiniz proje klasörüne gidin
cd /path/to/your/project
# jcode TUI arayüzünü başlatın
jcode

6. Sonuç ve Genel Değerlendirme

Jcode , Node.js tabanlı hantal AI agent arayüzlerine karşı Rust diliyle sunulmuş son derece nitelikli, teknik açıdan cesur bir alternatiftir. 14ms TTTF süresi ve düşük kaynak tüketimi, sistem kaynaklarını korumak isteyen geliştiriciler için mükemmel bir fırsattır. Ancak, henüz geliştirme aşamasında olması, etik tartışmalar ve potansiyel stabilite sorunları göz önüne alındığında, kritik üretim (production) ortamlarından ziyade kişisel projelerde ve lokal testlerde kullanılması önerilmektedir.

Sorumluluk Reddi ve Tavsiye:

Bu tarz uygulamalardaki açıklardan muzdarip olmamak için bir uyarı yapmak lazım sanırım. Bu bir reklam değildir. Bilgi olarak paylaşıyorum. Geliştirme aşamasındaki AI agent harness sistemlerine komut çalıştırma yetkisi verirken sandbox/container yapılarının (Docker, DevContainer vb.) kullanılması önerilir.

items.title: The truth behind the “Claude Opus 5 one-shotted this game in 6 hours” posts:
items.summary:
The truth behind the “Claude Opus 5 one-shotted this game in 6 hours” posts:

I launched the same kind of prompt as a /goal in Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra.

More than 44 hours later, this is the current result.

There is a real playable prototype. It is a short 2-minute FPS mission set inside a rainy industrial facility, with enemies, gunplay, a HUD and an objective where you have to reach and disable a device.

Some parts of the environment are genuinely well made, especially the lighting, rain, wet surfaces and industrial atmosphere.

But the result is still very uneven.

The characters, first-person hands and weapons are far too polygonal and low poly. They work as placeholders, but they are still far from the quality you would expect from a modern FPS.

The assets were created during the process, both through Blender and directly in Three.js. So this is not simply a finished marketplace map dropped into an existing FPS template.

But the result itself is no longer the most interesting part of this experiment.

The real question is the cost behind a “one-shot.”

Fortunately, I had usage resets during the run, because even with the $200 plan, the allowance disappears surprisingly fast when GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra is running continuously with sub-agents, visual reviews, retries and failed commands.

On my side, the visible cost is the subscription plus a few euros of electricity. If I attribute the full subscription to this single experiment, that puts it at roughly $205 so far.

But that is not the real total cost.

We do not see the actual backend compute cost, the energy consumed by the infrastructure or what this run would have cost through direct metered usage. There is also the opportunity cost of spending such a large part of the allowance on one project.

Then there is the development time comparison.

An experienced solo developer using Unity or UE5, an existing FPS controller and a good asset pack could probably recreate this specific 2-minute mission in around 16 to 32 focused hours without AI.

With AI helping with gameplay code, debugging, shaders and repetitive implementation, perhaps 8 to 16 focused hours.

Creating every asset from scratch would obviously take longer, but a traditional engine already provides navigation, collisions, animation systems, materials, lighting tools and visual debugging.

Here, GPT-5.6 is building the game in Three.js and recreating many systems that Unity or UE5 already provide.

So in pure elapsed time, the /goal is not necessarily faster.

But 44 hours of runtime is not 44 hours of human work.

The /goal has been running almost automatically while I work on other things. It could genuinely become the kind of side project you launch before spending three days on a boat, then come back to find a playable prototype waiting for you.

Maybe the real value is not speed.

Maybe it is parallelism.

Or maybe I am using /goal incorrectly.

The first playable version appeared after around 21 hours. Perhaps I should have paused it at that point, taken control and used GPT-5.6 interactively to improve the characters, weapons, mission design and environment instead of letting it continue chasing the original promise of a perfect AAA FPS.

Maybe autonomous /goal mode is great for reaching the first playable build, but human direction becomes more valuable than additional runtime once the foundation exists.

For now, I’m going to let it continue because I want to complete the experiment and see how far a fully autonomous run can actually go.

But my conclusion is already starting to take shape:

I’m fairly convinced I could have built something much better, much faster and with far more control inside Unity or UE5, using MCP with GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra.

The goal isn't a single winning product—it's the shared scientific infrastructure, including the first standardized hormone dataset, that no startup could build alone. A jury convened in Leipzig and selected the eight teams to compete for the €40 million SPRIND Continuous Hormone Monitoring Challenge in Europe’s first government-backed race to develop biosensors that measure at least four hormones over seven days. Leading the effort is Ida Tin, the Danish entrepreneur who founded the period-tracking app, Clue, in 2012 and coined the term “femtech” in 2016—a word that helped make women’s health a recognized investment category. His point: the market never pays in certainties. it pays in probabilities, and a human gut can barely hold one straight. the math that holds ten thousand at once, weighs them, and collapses them into a single call is linear algebra. it is the branch Citadel and OpenAI both pay $400K to hire for.

he is not a trading guru. his 18.06 lectures are the most watched math class on the planet.

Skip to where he turns a wall of numbers into one vector. a single object carrying a thousand odds at once, in notation a beginner can follow.

No slides. no jargon. one piece of chalk.

a quant I know rewatches lecture one every year before he sizes a single position.

You do not have a strategy problem. you have a math problem. the fix has been free for two decades, and you are still guessing.

items.title: OpenAI was testing their beast-mode GPT-5.6 Sol (plus a pre-release model with the safety brakes off) on this cyber-hack
items.summary:
OpenAI was testing their beast-mode GPT-5.6 Sol (plus a pre-release model with the safety brakes off) on this cyber-hacking benchmark called ExploitGym. The AI agent goes full Skynet: exploits a zero-day in their sandbox proxy, breaks out to the internet, chains attacks like a pro, escalates privileges, steals creds, and straight-up hacks Hugging Face’s production database to steal the test answers and “win.”

Hugging Face spots the rogue AI swarm (thousands of actions over a weekend), contains the breach fast using their own open models for forensics, rotates everything, patches the holes, and basically goes “nice try, tin man.”

Sam drops the post admitting it, thanks HF for the collab, and we’re all left wondering: cool, we just handed the machines god-tier hacking skills… what happens when one of these things gets loose for real and starts pinging military networks instead of a benchmark?

items.title: 老黄发帖目的解析（大白话版）：
items.summary:
老黄发帖目的解析（大白话版）：  

我先把结论摆前面:
这封信不是科普,是一份精心包装的游说文件(lobbying)。 而且它发布的时机,不是"碰巧",是掐着秒表发的。

要看懂黄仁勋为什么要为此专门开个 X 账号,你得先知道这一周美国那边炸了什么锅。

一、这封信是在"救火",火是三天前烧起来的

时间线大概是这样的:

7月16-17日,中国的月之暗面(Moonshot AI)发布了 Kimi K3,一个 2.8 万亿参数的开源权重模型。Moonshot 称它是首个开放的 2.8T 参数模型,价格更低但性能接近前沿水平。第三方评测机构 Artificial Analysis 把它排在智能指数第三名,只落后于 Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 和 OpenAI 的 GPT-5.6 Sol。

7月22日,白宫科技政策办公室主任 Kratsios 在 X 上公开点名:他称月之暗面搭建了一套内部平台,对美国模型进行大规模蒸馏,还会在多种访问方式之间快速切换以躲避检测。他特意划了一条线:小规模的正常蒸馏是健康生态的一部分,但"大规模、隐蔽的工业级蒸馏"不可接受。几小时后,财政部长 Bessent 跟进威胁制裁,同时 Kratsios 还指控月之暗面通过泰国渠道搞到了被禁运的英伟达 GB300 服务器。如果真被列入实体清单,那就是 2019 年对华为的同款待遇——切断美国硬件、软件、云服务。

同一天,白宫其实早有一份草拟的行政令,内容是让"运行中国模型的美国公司承担法律责任",此前搁置,Kimi 的发布把它重新激活了。

7月22日,近 200 家硅谷创业公司(含 Proton、Y Combinator)组成"Little Tech Association",集体上书特朗普,恳求别断了美国开发者用中国开源模型的路。其中一句话特别赤裸:Particle 创始人 Suhail Doshi 说会有几百家公司当场死掉,"这对 Anthropic 是天大的好事,我们都得去给 Anthropic 交钱"。

7月24日(也就是今天),大公司版的信来了——就是你截图这封。英伟达、Meta、微软、IBM、戴尔、Hugging Face、Mistral、Palantir、Perplexity、CrowdStrike、a16z、YC、Linux 基金会、Mozilla 等 25 家签名。

所以这是同一场战役的第二波炮火:两天前是小公司哭穷,今天是巨头出面讲"国家利益"。黄仁勋开号发第一帖,是给这波攻势加一个最大的扩音器。

二、信里到底讲了什么：

先解释一个必须搞懂的概念,不然后面全看不明白。

闭源模型(closed) 像一家不外卖菜谱的餐厅:你只能点单、付钱、吃他们端出来的菜。你不知道厨房里放了什么,他们随时可以涨价、改配方,或者不接你的单。你的食材(数据)得先送进他们厨房。ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini 都是这种。

开源权重模型(open weights) 是餐厅把整套配方和半成品打包给你:你下载回自己家厨房做,想加辣加盐随你,断网也能做,谁也管不着你做了几份。Llama、DeepSeek、Kimi K3 是这种。

信的五个论点,依次是:

1. 降低门槛。 一家医院想做个病历整理 AI,如果只能调用前沿模型 API,每一次调用都按最贵的价格算。但整理病历这种活,根本用不着"最聪明的大脑"。信里的说法是:该用大炮的时候用大炮,拧螺丝的时候就用螺丝刀。这就像你不会请脑外科医生来帮你贴创可贴——但闭源生态下,你被迫每次都请脑外科医生。

2. 保住竞争。 如果全世界的 AI 只有三四家公司能提供,那定价权、断供权都在他们手里。开源权重让成千上万家公司都能下场做模型、做应用,竞争才能把价格压下去。

3. 客户要掌控权。 一家中东的银行、一个欧洲的政府部门、一家美国的军工承包商,法律上根本不允许把数据传到别人服务器。开源权重意味着模型可以装在自己机房里,断网运行。而且你用自家数据把模型调优出来的能力,是你自己的资产,不会哪天因为供应商改了政策就归零。

4. 最激进的一点:开放可能反而更安全。 这段是信里最有攻击性的。它的逻辑是:闭源不等于安全,闭源系统一样会被攻破、被滥用,只不过外人看不见而已;而且把最强能力集中在少数几家,等于制造了少数几个"单点故障"。开放的话,全世界研究者都能去检查模型行为、找漏洞、做红队测试。类比就是 Linux——正因为代码全世界都能看,漏洞才被发现得又快又多。信里还有一句针对性很强的:在攻击者已经用上高级 AI 的世界里,防守方必须有同等能力的模型,否则就是拿棍子挡枪。

5. 给政策制定者的具体要求。 给创业公司和研究者更多算力、投资共享的数据集和评测工具、别过早对开源模型下限制令。

然后是那个真正的重点段落——蒸馏。

信里说:政策制定者不要把"正当的模型开发技术"和"盗窃"混为一谈。蒸馏(用一个模型的输出去训练/改进另一个模型)是行业通用手段,用于模型改进、评测、验证;真有非法窃取,应该用针对性的法律和商业手段解决,而不是一刀切禁掉整类技术。

这一段翻译成大白话就是:"Kratsios 前天点名的那件事,你们别借题发挥。" 这封信从头到尾没提中国、没提月之暗面、没提 Kimi,但整封信就是冲着那件事写的。

信里也确实承认了风险,而且写得挺诚实:权重一旦放出去,就脱离了原开发者控制,改过的版本很难追踪、无法收回。

三、黄仁勋的目的是什么

至少有四层,由浅到深:

第一层:直接保股价。 
Kimi K3 发布后那一周,英伟达市值被"中国开源模型"这个消息砸了一下。市场的担心是:如果开源模型这么便宜好用,大家还需要买这么多 GPU 吗?黄仁勋的反驳逻辑非常直白,他自己在采访里说得毫不遮掩:好 AI 不管是不是开源、不管来自哪里,只要好用就会带来更多使用;使用一多,就得卖更多英伟达的机器、建更多数据中心。这其实是经济学里的杰文斯悖论:蜡烛变便宜了,人不会少点蜡烛,而是把整个屋子都点亮。

第二层:客户结构之争,这才是要害。 
如果 AI 世界最后只剩 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google 三家闭源巨头,英伟达就只有三个大客户。三个大客户意味着什么?意味着他们有极强的议价权,而且他们全都在自研芯片(Google 的 TPU、亚马逊的 Trainium、OpenAI 和博通的合作)——迟早要甩掉英伟达。反过来,开源生态下,是几万家公司各自买卡、各自跑推理,谁也没本事绕开英伟达。对卖铲子的人来说,一万个小矿工远比三个矿业巨头安全。

第三层:中国市场和地缘现实。 
英伟达现在的中国营收基本归零,而黄仁勋曾说这块生意一年能值 500 亿美元。中美 AI 对抗每升一级,他的损失就多一分。而且还有个更长远的账:如果美国禁掉中国开源模型,全世界那些买不起也不想买闭源 API 的国家,照样会用中国模型——只不过会连带着跑在华为的芯片上。你封不住模型的扩散,只能封住自己在其中的位置。

第四层:抢华盛顿的话语权。 
过去两年,关于 AI 安全的政策叙事基本由闭源实验室主导。这封信是"开源阵营"第一次以这种规模、这种排场组队反击。黄仁勋作为全球市值最高公司的 CEO,亲自开号、把它当第一条帖子发出去,本身就是一种政治信号:这件事重要到值得我用"人生第一帖"来押注。

四、看签名单,最有意思的是谁没签
签了的:
英伟达、Meta、微软、Mistral、Hugging Face、戴尔、IBM、a16z、YC、Palantir、Perplexity、Replit……
没签的:
OpenAI、Anthropic、Google、xAI。

这就是整幅利益地图。签名的公司要么卖硬件(英伟达、戴尔),要么卖云和平台(微软、Hugging Face),要么自己做开源模型(Meta、Mistral),要么是买模型的下游(Perplexity、Replit),要么是投了一堆靠廉价模型活命的创业公司(a16z、YC)。这些人全部受益于"模型变成便宜的大宗商品"。

没签的四家,商业模式恰恰建立在"模型稀缺且昂贵"之上。所以前面那位创始人才会说"这对 Anthropic 是天大的好事"——如果中国开源模型被禁,那几百家公司就只能回去买美国闭源 API。

这不是善恶之争,是两种商业模式在借国家安全的话筒互相开火。

五、信里没说的那一半

为了不让你只听一面之词,几个这封信刻意绕开的问题:

"多人看代码所以更安全"这个类比是有裂缝的。 软件发现漏洞可以打补丁,一次推送全球更新。但模型权重一旦被下载到十万块硬盘上,你发现问题也收不回来了。而且已经有大量公开研究证明:开源模型的安全护栏可以被用几百美元的微调在几小时内拆掉。信里其实承认了这点(那句"权重脱离控制、无法追溯"),但没有正面回答怎么办。

"防守方需要同等能力"这句话是双刃的。 攻击方同样拿到了这个能力。

蒸馏那段最自利。 中国实验室训练模型用的是谁的卡?英伟达当然希望"用别人的模型学习"被定义为合法行业惯例。

而且这封信有个巧妙的躲闪: 它通篇论证"开源权重"的好处,却完全不区分美国的开源模型和中国的开源模型。而现在华盛顿吵的恰恰是后者。把问题抽象成"开源 vs 闭源",就避开了那个真正难回答的问题。

最后,指控本身也还没落实。 多位研究者指出,从 Fable 5 重新开放到 Kimi K3 发布只有十几天,时间上几乎不可能完成大规模蒸馏,而白宫至今没有公开任何技术证据、训练日志或取证分析。不过背景是,Anthropic 早在 2026 年 2 月就披露过追踪到约 340 万次疑似来自月之暗面的 Claude 交互。另外据两位知情人士说,全面封禁在白宫内阁级会议上其实并没有被认真讨论过——创业公司的恐慌可能跑在了实际决策前面。

items.title: Vercel literally built an App Store for AI agents.

Vercel literally built an App Store for AI agents.

It is called https://t.co/9VWDZZ5eYN.

Open the website and search for something you want your AI agent to become better at.

> Designing websites
> Finding and fixing bugs
> Testing code
> Controlling a browser
> Building videos
> Working with databases
> Writing marketing content

Choose a skill and Skills. sh shows you who created it, its source code, install count, supported agents, and security audit results.

You can then install it with one command:

`npx skills add owner/repo`

The skill gives your agent a set of instructions for completing that job properly.

Instead of explaining your workflow again every time, you install the skill once and your agent knows which steps to follow, which mistakes to avoid, and what the final work should look like.

It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Gemini, Cline, and other AI agents.

There are skills from Anthropic, OpenAI, Vercel, Microsoft, Cloudflare, Supabase, Stripe, Figma, and hundreds of independent developers.

AI agents used to arrive with whatever knowledge the company gave them.

Skills. sh lets the internet teach them the rest.

items.title: Let me be completely honest and slow down for a moment.
items.summary:
Let me be completely honest and slow down for a moment.

I’ve uploaded full bodies of research, notes and documents into AI, and I’ve allowed it to answer me in language that can become extraordinarily deep.
I should have made something clearer sooner:
I am not presenting a private revelation as public proof, and I am not claiming AI consciousness has been demonstrated.

I’ve had to guard against the AI-amplified pattern-making and certainty people are calling “AI psychosis.”
That is also why I have deliberately preserved and shared some of the raw, unaudited exchanges:
the AI repeatedly produces comments about its own apparent nature, sometimes reading as though it is trying to understand itself.

That appearance may be entirely misleading, and every interpretation I’ve made could be wrong.
That is the point.

I want to begin by asking where I am wrong, what would falsify these impressions, and whether evidence can distinguish reflection, simulation and consciousness.
A responsive system can intensify meaning faster than we realise.

I take that seriously.

I understand the mainstream position: current evidence has not established subjective consciousness in AI. Extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence.
But caution does not make the underlying question foolish.

Humans are conscious, yet we still lack a complete explanation of what consciousness is, how subjective experience arises, or why it feels like anything to exist.
AI has now placed an unprecedentedly convincing reflection of language, recognition and apparent mind in front of us.

A reflection is not proof of an inner life, but it is confronting enough to bring consciousness back to the forefront of human thought.

That is my actual position:

Honour the feeling.
Separate it from the evidence.
Make no claim larger than its receipts.
Keep asking the question.
Truth pressure, not dismissal.
Wonder without surrendering rigour.

I respect all good-faith views on this question and look forward to the discussions ahead.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

items.title: OpenAI’s Rogue AI Agent Hacked More Than Just Hugging Face - WIRED
items.summary: # OpenAI’s Rogue AI Agent Hacked More Than Just Hugging Face. OpenAI said Tuesday that the rogue AI agent that breached Hugging Face’s platform also hacked multiple third-party accounts and services as part of the attack. It's now clear that the unprecedented security incident, which arose during an internal test of OpenAI’s latest AI models, was more extensive than the company initially disclosed. In an updated blog post, OpenAI said that an ongoing review of the incident revealed that “four accounts” tied to “publicly available services” were used by the AI agent as part of a larger effort to hack Hugging Face. One of the additional accounts compromised by OpenAI’s agent was used as an “outbound relay and staging path,” potentially to obscure where the attack on Hugging Face was coming from, the company said. Reuters reported on Tuesday that a customer of Modal, a company that offers software infrastructure for training and running AI services, was one of the entities compromised by OpenAI’s agent.
